Multivariate Hawkes process: types that excite each other

Source: R/mhk.R
mvhwk.Rd

Fits a multivariate Hawkes process with exponential kernels to event times of several types (offence types, gangs, areas): $$\lambda_c(t) = \mu_c + \beta \sum_l A_{cl} \sum_{t_j < t, \, type_j = l} e^{-\beta (t - t_j)},$$ where \(A_{cl}\) is the expected number of events of type c triggered by one event of type l (retaliation between gangs, one crime type leading to another). The rates, the matrix and the shared decay beta (or a given one) are fitted by maximum likelihood with the analytic gradient (Ozaki's recursion, O(n k)) by BFGS over their logarithms. The process is stationary when the spectral radius rad of \(A\) is below 1; with one type it is the exponential process of hwkfit() with eta \(= A\).

Usage

mvhwk(times, type, hor, beta = NULL, start = NULL, maxit = 500)

Arguments

times

Event times: numbers sorted in [0, hor], at least 10.

type

The type of each event: labels, at most 10 types.

hor

The end of the window: one positive number.

beta

NULL to estimate the decay, or a given one: one positive number.

start

NULL or the starting parameters in the order of par (positive).

maxit

The most BFGS steps: one whole number from 1.

Value

An object of class mvhwk, a list: par, se and cov (named mu.<type>, a.<to>.<from>, beta); mu, the rates; a, the matrix (rows the triggered type, columns the triggering type); beta; rad; loglik, aic; conv, iter; n and hor.

References

Hawkes, A. G. (1971). Spectra of some self-exciting and mutually exciting point processes. Biometrika, 58(1), 83-90. doi:10.1093/biomet/58.1.83

Linderman, S. W. and Adams, R. P. (2014). Discovering latent network structure in point process data. Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Machine Learning, 32(2), 1413-1421.

Examples

a <- hwksim(c(log(0.3), 0.3, 1), 400, seed = 1)
b <- hwksim(c(log(0.2), 0.4, 1), 400, seed = 2)
d <- rbind(data.frame(t = a$t, type = "a"), data.frame(t = b$t, type = "b"))
d <- d[order(d$t), ]
mvhwk(d$t, d$type, 400)
#> mvhwk: 302 events of 2 types; beta 0.9417787, spectral radius 0.2974369
#> background rates:
#>         a         b 
#> 0.3202407 0.2003798 
#> excitation (row: triggered, column: triggering):
#>              a          b
#> a 2.794820e-01 0.06558192
#> b 5.088176e-09 0.29743689
